questions.stem: Why is electricity transmitted at high voltage across the National Grid?

options.text: High voltage makes the electricity travel faster through the cables
High voltage reduces the current, which reduces energy lost as heat in the cables
High voltage is needed because homes are very far from power stations
High voltage prevents the cables from breaking

questions.explanation: For a given power (P = IV), increasing the voltage means the current can be reduced. Since power loss in the cables is P = I squared R, a lower current dramatically reduces energy wasted as heat. Doubling the voltage halves the current and reduces losses by a factor of four.

questions.stem: What is the role of a step-up transformer in the National Grid?

options.text: It reduces the voltage for safe use in homes
It increases the voltage at the power station for efficient long-distance transmission
It stores electricity for peak demand

questions.explanation: A step-up transformer at the power station increases the voltage from around 25 kV to 400 kV for transmission. This high voltage means a lower current is needed, reducing energy losses in the cables over long distances.
